features.title: Curated Webb Gallery
features.body: Webb's greatest images — the Cosmic Cliffs, the Pillars of Creation, deep fields and more — grouped into collections and shown with their real captions, credits, distances, and sky coordinates. Search for any target.

features.title: Where Is Webb
features.body: A live status dashboard for the telescope itself: how long it's been in space, its orbit a million-plus miles away at Lagrange Point 2, and the astonishing gap between its sun-facing side and its supercooled instruments.

features.title: 4K Wallpapers
features.body: Save any Webb image as a 4K wallpaper for your iPhone, iPad, Mac, or Apple TV — straight from the source, at full resolution. Part of Solar Beam Premium.

features.title: Picture of the Day
features.body: NASA picks one image of the cosmos every day. Solar Beam puts it front and center with plain-language, AI-powered facts so you understand what you're looking at.

features.title: Asteroid Tracker
features.body: See what's passing Earth in real time: how close each asteroid comes, how fast it moves, and the size of impact it would leave. Charts sort the dangerous from the safe — always free.

features.title: Everywhere, one purchase
features.body: A native app on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, and Vision Pro — with a menu bar ticker on Mac, Ambient Mode on every screen, and Spatial Scenes on Vision Pro. Buy once, with Family Sharing.

howItWorks.body: Get Solar Beam free from the App Store on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, or Vision Pro. No account, no purchase — today's NASA picture is always free.
Land in the curated Webb gallery and the live "Where Is Webb" dashboard, with the daily picture and the asteroid tracker a tap away.
Unlock Solar Beam Premium for the complete Webb gallery, 4K wallpapers, Ambient Mode, years of past pictures, and unlimited AI facts — by subscription or a one-time lifetime purchase.

faq.q: What makes Solar Beam's James Webb gallery special?
faq.a: It's a curated gallery of the telescope's best images — not a raw data dump. Each image comes with its real caption, credit, distance, instruments, and sky coordinates, grouped into collections (nebulae, galaxies, deep fields, the solar system, and more), and you can search for any target. A live "Where Is Webb" dashboard shows the telescope's status in real time.

Solar Beam is a single universal app for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, and Vision Pro. One purchase covers them all, with Family Sharing. It's native on each — a menu bar ticker on Mac, Ambient Mode everywhere, and Spatial Scenes on Vision Pro.

faq.q: How much does Solar Beam cost?
faq.a: Solar Beam is free to download, and a new NASA picture of the day is always free. Solar Beam Premium is optional — it adds the complete Webb gallery, 4K wallpapers and full-resolution downloads, Ambient Mode, the complete archive of past pictures, and unlimited AI facts.

faq.q: What do I get for free versus Premium?
faq.a: Free covers today's picture, the live asteroid tracker, the "Where Is Webb" dashboard, a taste of the curated Webb gallery, and a rolling 30-day window of past pictures. Premium unlocks the full Webb gallery, 4K wallpapers and downloads, Ambient Mode, years of archived pictures, Spatial Scenes on Vision Pro, and unlimited AI-generated facts.

faq.q: Is there a subscription or in-app purchase?
faq.a: Only if you want more. The app is free; Solar Beam Premium is available either as a subscription (with a free trial on the annual plan) or a one-time lifetime unlock. The daily picture and asteroid tracker stay free either way.

faq.q: Where do the images and data come from?
faq.a: From NASA's public APIs and the ESA/Webb archive: the Astronomy Picture of the Day, James Webb Space Telescope imagery (ESA/Webb, CC BY 4.0), and near-Earth object data. Solar Beam is an independent app and is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA or ESA.

faq.q: Can I really set Webb images as wallpaper?
faq.a: Yes. With Premium, save any Webb image at 4K — desktop and mobile sizes — and set it as your wallpaper on iPhone, iPad, Mac, or Apple TV. Free sharing is at display resolution.
